t: #2380 Time Needed to Rearrange a Binary String
o: Every second, every "01" simultaneously flips to "10", so 1s march left and 0s march right until the string looks like `111...000`. In "0110101" the leftmost 0 must travel past four 1s, taking 4 seconds — matching the expected output. In "11100" nothing moves, so the answer is 0. With n ≤ 1000 a brute-force simulation passes easily, but the follow-up asks for O(n). Constraints imply we just need the finishing time of the slowest particle.
k: The process is equivalent to particles (0s) drifting right at 1 cell/second, never reordering.
A zero's displacement equals the number of 1s originally to its right; the answer is the maximum displacement.
Simulating round-by-round is O(n²) but trivially correct — good as a sanity baseline.

a.i: Directly apply the rule: scan for "01" occurrences, replace them all at once, count rounds until none remain. It mirrors the problem statement exactly, so it is easy to trust.
s: Repeat: build the next string by replacing every "01" with "10" (scan left to right, greedily matching).
If the string did not change, stop; otherwise increment the counter.
a.t: O(n²) — up to n rounds, each an O(n) scan; fine for n ≤ 1000.

a.i: Zeros never cross each other, and the k-th zero (left to right) finishes at position n−m+k−1 where m is the zero count. Its travel time is exactly the number of 1s to its right, and simultaneous motion means the answer is the maximum such travel over all zeros.
s: Scan the string once, maintaining a running count of 1s seen so far.
When a '0' is found, the number of 1s to its right is (total ones − ones so far); update the answer with this value.
a.t: O(n) — a single scan plus one count.

w: Use the simulation to explain your reasoning in an interview, then present the O(n) one-pass for the follow-up. Pitfall: forgetting that all swaps happen simultaneously (so you cannot reuse the mutated string mid-round in the brute force). Edge cases: all-equal strings (answer 0), single character. Follow-ups: prove why max displacement suffices, or generalize to parallel-update cellular automata.
